text:
[NLFC.7.1] Every libds entry point reports the same way: one returned value
carrying a machine-readable status and an optional human-readable detail.
That follows from libds holding no global state at all
([NLFC.1.3]), and it is what keeps two engines in one process independent in
their error reporting as well as their data.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| status | the outcome; zero is success, errors are negative, and the taxonomy is [NLFC.7.4] |
| detail | a message for a human -- a log line, a fault report. **May be absent**, and is borrowed when present ([NLFC.7.2]) |

The split is the point: branch on the status, never on the text. `detail`
exists to make a failure diagnosable and is free to change wording, so a
caller that parses it has coupled itself to something that carries no
guarantee. A caller that formats it must also tolerate its absence.
